clue.text: Sweet drink is in front of soda dispenser

indicators.note: says the drink comes before the sweet in the answer

parts.note: to drink slowly is to sip
hon, short for honey, is a sweet term of endearment

explanation.surface: A sugary drink seems to be served ahead of the fizzy water machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective for the drink, but it is a term of endearment; 'is in front of' puts the drink first.
explanation.definitionFit: A soda siphon is a pressurised bottle that squirts carbonated water.

clue.text: Immovable plug almost on top

indicators.note: says the plug word loses its last letter

parts.note: to stop a hole is to plug it
a lid is the top of a container

explanation.surface: A plug that nearly fits sits on top and will not budge.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid describes someone impassive and unmoved by emotion.

clue.text: Likely complication of pill abuse

indicators.note: a complication is a tangle, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A probable side effect of misusing tablets.
explanation.definitionFit: Plausible means credible or seeming probable.

clue.text: Surfer having crack, skipping first Ecstasy

indicators.note: says the first appearance of the drug letter is left out

parts.note: a crack is a quip, a short witty joke
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: A beach surfer on crack who has given up Ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' and 'Ecstasy' suggest drugs, but crack is a joke, a ONE-LINER, whose first E is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: An on-liner surfs the internet, being connected online.

clue.text: Tragic lover's family united in composite photo

indicators.note: says the abbreviation sits inside the photo word

parts.note: a montage is a picture assembled from several images
U is the usual abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A star-crossed lover's relatives pose together in a collage picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo, Shakespeare's tragic lover, belongs to the Verona house that feuds with the Capulets.

clue.text: Birtwistle sheds irritability after wrong viol note: he requested more

indicators.note: places the reduced name after the viol and note letters
a wrong arrangement means the instrument's letters are reordered

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: says the bad-temper letters are removed from the composer's name

parts.note: bile means bad temper or irritability

explanation.surface: Composer Harrison Birtwistle calms down after a badly played viol note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns VIOL into OLIV; 'sheds' takes B, I, L, E out of BIRTWISTLE, leaving RTWIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's orphan famously asks the workhouse master for a second helping of gruel.

clue.text: Something exciting below opening of the pocket

indicators.note: in a down clue puts the exciting word under the initial letter
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a rouser is something that stirs people up

explanation.surface: Something thrilling sits under the opening of a pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pocket' looks like a noun but is the verb: to trouser money is British slang for pocketing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to take money for oneself, often dishonestly.

clue.text: Complaint in which body part's more than half twisted

indicators.note: says the first three of the five letters are turned backwards

parts.note: an organ is a part of the body

explanation.surface: A grievance about a body part that has been badly wrenched.
explanation.walkthrough: Only ORG is reversed, giving GRO, and AN stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: A groan is a sound of protest, so it can mean a grumble or grievance.

clue.text: Low-maintenance aspect of literacy's aesthetically uplifting

indicators.note: uplifting says the hidden letters are read backwards
an aspect is one part of something, so a portion of these words gives the letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Reading well can be artistically uplifting with little effort.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Low-maintenance aspect' as definition; 'aspect of' is the hiding signal, and the answer is an adjective, not an aspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy-care fabrics or gardens need little attention or upkeep.

clue.text: A choice word at length accepted by expert, one considered infallible

parts.note: or is the word that offers a choice between alternatives

indicators.note: says the length letter is taken inside the expert word

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A grammar note: a word of choice, accepted at length by an authority who cannot be wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient oracles, like Delphi's, gave pronouncements regarded as beyond error; hence any unquestioned authority.

clue.text: Drop back before short stir, lacking courage

indicators.note: places the reversed drop ahead of the shortened stir
asks for the word for drop to be read backwards

parts.note: to omit something is to drop it

indicators.note: says the stir word loses its final letter

parts.note: to rouse is to stir up

explanation.surface: Someone timid falls back rather than stirring things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses OMIT to TIMO; 'short' cuts ROUSE to ROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Timorous is a synonym of timid, describing someone without bravery.

clue.text: Lying, popular from the time of bible studies

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
since means from a given time onwards
RE is religious education, the British school subject covering bible studies

explanation.surface: A sceptic's view: popular since scripture classes, and dishonest throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education) is the British school subject once commonly called scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: An insincere person is not being truthful, so the adjective fits a deceitful remark.

clue.text: What makes Ireland seem exotic, with latitude for name?

definitions.text: What makes Ireland seem exotic, with latitude for name?

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange, so these letters are rearranged
says one letter stands in place of the other

explanation.surface: A travel writer's question: what gives Ireland its exotic flavour, latitude perhaps?
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the name letter for the latitude one in IRELAND SEEM and rearranging gives the answer, itself a poetic name for Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland's poetic nickname comes from its green landscape, which exotic language romanticises.

clue.text: Very enjoyable after reduction of noise

parts.note: so is an intensifier meaning very

indicators.note: says the enjoyable word is trimmed of its last letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant or enjoyable

explanation.surface: Something becomes really pleasant once the racket is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduction of noise' reads as one phrase, but 'of noise' is the definition and 'after reduction' cuts the last letter from the enjoyable word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic means relating to sound, the physical phenomenon that noise is.

clue.text: Bishop and religious fraternity volunteer a rough-haired companion?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a monastic order is a religious brotherhood
a Terrier is a member of Britain's Territorial Army, a volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A churchman and his brotherhood send along a scruffy volunteer as a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: A Terrier, slang for a Territorial Army member, is a part-time volunteer soldier in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Border terrier is a small dog breed with a wiry, rough coat, kept as a pet.

clue.text: Poor condition of Leith Hall after renovation

indicators.note: renovation reworks a building, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A Scottish country house falls into decline after being done up.
explanation.walkthrough: Leith Hall is a historic house in Aberdeenshire, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unwell means one's bodily state is bad.

clue.text: Lender perhaps welcoming credit, one trying hard to clean up

definitions.text: one trying hard to clean up

indicators.note: says the lender word takes the credit letters inside it

parts.note: a subber is one who subs, or advances money, an example of a lender
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A moneylender takes on credit while a hard worker tidies up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who scrubs works vigorously at cleaning.

clue.text: Melting out ice and splitting fossil fuel with mixed forms

indicators.note: says the rearranged letters break the fuel word apart

parts.note: coal is the classic fossil fuel

indicators.note: melting ice loses its shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A climate scene: ice melts while fossil fuel is broken up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Melting' rearranges OUT ICE AND; 'splitting' puts those letters between the first two and last two of the fuel. 'forms' are British school classes.
explanation.definitionFit: A school for boys and girls together teaches mixed classes, the British word for which is forms.

clue.text: Send wacky timeless object wrapped in one from Paris

indicators.note: places the shortened object inside the French word

parts.note: une is French for one

indicators.note: says the time letter is removed from the object word

parts.note: a thing is an object

explanation.surface: An eternal artefact gift-wrapped by a Parisian drives someone crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' removes T (time) from THING, leaving HING.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhinge someone is to drive them mad, making them unbalanced.

clue.text: New bond set up the woman's option to exclude both?

indicators.note: in a down clue means the bond word reads upwards

parts.note: a tie is a bond
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A fresh connection lets her rule out both possibilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Choosing 'not one nor the other' rules out both alternatives offered.

clue.text: Treatment for ticker tape lacking copy in colour

indicators.note: puts what is left inside the colour word

parts.note: a stain colours something

indicators.note: says the copy word is taken out of the tape word

parts.note: to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: Ticker tape without a copy, printed in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ticker tape' reads as one phrase, but 'ticker' is slang for the heart; 'lacking' leaves T from TAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Statins are cholesterol-lowering drugs prescribed to protect the heart.

clue.text: Universal shock over Dickensian name

parts.note: U is the British film classification for universal viewing

indicators.note: says the hair word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it

explanation.surface: A film-studio jolt delivered about a character from Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' suggests surprise but means a mop of hair; 'over' reverses HAIR to RIAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Uriah Heep is the fawning clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield.

clue.text: Is doing permanent damage, promoting current religious leaders

indicators.note: in a down clue means the current letter is moved higher up

parts.note: maims means injures lastingly
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Clerics are blamed for causing lasting harm by pushing a modern line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'modern' but is I, moved up to the front of MAIMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Imams lead prayers in mosques, so they are Islamic religious leaders.

clue.text: Loss of resistance in period beset by depression

indicators.note: says the combined letters are surrounded by the depression word

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow or depression

indicators.note: puts the resistance letter inside the period word

parts.note: time is a period
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A gloomy spell surrounds a stretch of weakened resistance, ending in loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests low mood but means a dent; 'in' makes TRIME, which 'beset by' puts inside DENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Detriment means harm or damage, so it can stand for a loss suffered.

clue.text: As one says, charred skeleton remains dandy once in Bath

indicators.note: tells us the answer is pronounced like the remains phrase

parts.note: bone ash is what is left when bones are burnt

explanation.surface: A grim cremation detail somehow turns into a Georgian dandy in a spa town.
explanation.walkthrough: Beau Nash was the celebrated eighteenth-century master of ceremonies in Bath, the English spa city.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard 'Beau' Nash was a famous Georgian fashion leader who ruled society in Bath.

clue.text: Although learner, participating in game of cards

indicators.note: says the learner letter is placed inside the card game

parts.note: whist is a trick-taking card game
L is the learner-driver plate letter

explanation.surface: Though a novice, someone joins in a hand of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Whilst is the British variant of 'while', a conjunction meaning even though.

clue.text: At Oktoberfest, you must separate part with English brew

indicators.note: joins the English letter onto the end
says the German word splits the part word apart

parts.note: a role is a part in a play
Sie is the German for 'you', and Oktoberfest is Munich's beer festival

explanation.surface: A Munich drinker says you must leave the group and drink English beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosie Lee is Cockney rhyming slang for tea; 'brew' is a British word for a pot of tea, not beer.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang the name stands for tea, a brew in everyday British speech.

clue.text: Naughty child's primitive feature?

parts.note: Ur- is a prefix meaning primitive or original
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A mischievous child's face is described by its most basic trait.
explanation.definitionFit: An urchin is a scruffy, mischievous youngster.
